closingKeywordWhy: The issue's acceptance is a gap analysis delivered as 'wiring plus a documented gap list, not a second store'. This PR ships the re-runnable analysis (canary history gaps), the documented gap list G1-G6 (docs/guides/history-gaps.md), the reporter-to-history doc wiring (G4) and the /canary-clocktower skill. Filling G1-G3 changes the writers inside ts/src/history and is filed separately as #1125, not part of #610's acceptance.
assumptions: Issue premise verified against 47745970 before building: the store and its writer exist (history record, #538 closed); the real gap is field-level -- area, failure_category and tags are declared and read but written by no writer.

Human-answered fork: new module reading history's existing exports (ts/src/analysis/clocktower/), zero lines under ts/src/history/**; mounted as `canary history gaps` from the #988 engine registry beside `history trim`.
Brainstorming ran in autonomous mode: the EVALUATE questions D2-D8 in the proposal were self-answered with the recommended option instead of a human round.
Runtime command plus document (D2) rather than a static gap document, so the gap list stays re-measurable per adopter store.
Gate exit contract (D4): 0 all measured consumers fed, 1 dark/partial or unreadable store, 3 abstained on a missing or empty store; missing and empty are distinct reasons (D7).
A requirement with no applicable rows is 'unmeasured', never 'fed', and renders as a skipped entry (D6); failed-test scope covers status failed and flaky, mirroring the analyze engine.
A configured CANARY_HISTORY_DB_URL is analysed-around, not refused: the local store is read and the remote is named as skipped (D8).
Store flag is --path <store> (not the spec draft's --history): every engine command that reads or writes the store already uses --path.
Guide placed at docs/guides/history-gaps.md beside rewind/order guides rather than docs/history-gaps.md; spec updated.
Companion skill is thin (SKILL.md over `cli: canary history gaps`), following canary-batwoman; no persona YAML, since no test requires one.

Autopilot delegated planning to harness-planner and review to harness-code-reviewer; execution and verification were done by the lane agent directly (TDD with planted positives per key test) rather than by harness-task-executor/harness-verifier subagents, to keep ratchet measurement in one context.

First harness-code-reviewer pass returned Request Changes (C1, I1-I4 blocking). All fixed with TDD, plus I5, I6 and S1; every new predicate test was proved able to fail by a planted mutation (14 plants; the one that stayed green exposed a missing unknown-reporter case, which was added).

C1: screech split into screech-range (branch, commit_sha, timestamp per run) and screech-cluster (area, failure_category on hard failures only, mirroring screech's isFailure, which excludes flakes). Implemented as an optional per-requirement `where` filter.
I1: the area row is flaky-area (history flaky area column). `analyze area-health` is not a row: its engine hard-codes an empty row set, so it is documented as structurally dark (G7), not measured.

I5: rewind requires only its refusal fields (commit_sha not 'local', reporter_format in REPLAYABLE_RUNNERS, repo-relative test_file), imported from analysis/rewind/plan.ts. replay and start_index only degrade replay fidelity and were dropped as requirements.

I6: failure-categories (analyze common-failures) also requires error_text over failed and flaky tests; its failure_category denominator is not narrowed by error_text, so a store with no error text reads dark rather than unmeasured. `analyze spikes` left the surface: it reads rates, not categories. The Playwright reader drops error_text for flakes (G8), surfaced as partial.

S4 (lane's call): an opt-in consumer that is not fed (order-ttff without --order-plan) is a skipped entry with reason 'opt-in: not recorded with history record --order-plan', not a finding, so a store that never used the flag does not fail the gate.
Precedence unchanged: an unmeasured requirement still makes the whole consumer unmeasured even if another requirement is dark (existing tested rule, D6).

module-size grew 46291 -> 47148 (47091 before review fixes) with newViolations []; recorded in .harness/arch/allowances/feat-610-canary-clocktower.json against merge base de3f67f7 and the floor raised by scripts/refresh-arch-baseline.mjs.
Rebased twice onto a moving main (47745970 -> 32d80d07 -> de3f67f7), both clean. Ratchets measured in fresh detached worktrees of de3f67f7 and the head, removed afterwards.

The original lane worktree /Users/bs/Github/canary-fleet-610-clocktower was deleted mid-lane by a human disk cleanup (not by this lane); work resumed in /Users/bs/Github/canary-610-clocktower-resume from the intact branch ref.

Second harness-code-reviewer pass: Approve, no blocking findings. Its non-blocking suggestions 1-3 and 5 were taken test-first with planted positives: screech-range also requires a numeric run `failed` (redness.mjs isRed), order-ttff requires both TTFF estimates (ttff-report.ts), a partial opt-in consumer is a finding (only a dark one is skipped), and stale area-health wording was removed. Not taken: 4 (narrowing the category denominator by error_text, which would turn a dark consumer into an unmeasured one) and 6 (unchecked line citations in the mirror rows).
